meaningMnemonic: This radical swings like a monkey, howls like a wolf, and pounces like a leopard. You can almost hear the jungle chorus… This is the radical for animal !

It's the drunkard from before, but this time she's leaning on some kind of horizontal surface. Knowing her, it's probably the counter of a bar . Hopefully she's not causing too much trouble for the bar staff with her drunken antics.
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means part .
What do you call a prison for drops of water? A pool ! The water may not like being in there, but the rest of us sure appreciate it on a hot summer day.
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means public .
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means talent .

This is the radical for well — the kind you use to draw up water. Picture an old-timey stone well with wooden posts holding up a crank for reeling up your bucket! Pretty well built, huh? Well , well … Still can't see it? Try another view: picture a well seen from above. This one's got a square-shaped opening, 'cause that's what Japanese wells used to look like in the old days. Hope this one works well for you!

In a private place on the moon , you hide two spoon s that give you a special ability . It's the ability to predict the future! The private moon spoons reflect the knowledge of time and space into your brain. Now that's a cool ability! Hints I wish I had this kind of ability... maybe I'll go up to the moon and try to steal your spoons.
readingMnemonic: This ability to predict the future makes you famous and now everyone knows your name: No stradamus ( のう )! And now that people know about your name and special ability, everyone will love you! Hints Oh, you thought I was talking about that old Nostradamus, who also had the ability to predict things? Nah, you're way cooler than him.

meaningMnemonic: You put flowers on a cloud and call it art . Not everyone agrees that your flower cloud art is actually art, but you know it is. Hints Imagine piling up flowers on top of clouds to make your own unique art. It’s a fiddly business, because they keep falling through the clouds, but you get there in the end. Now step back and marvel at your work of flower cloud art.
readingMnemonic: Your beautiful art is going to be displayed at a gay ( げい ) club. Imagine the pride you feel about having your art on display. Hints Picture the gay club with your art displayed behind the bar. Fame and fortune are just around the corner, now.

meaningMnemonic: Rain makes up one part of this, and the rest is air or something. I imagine this is what people thought the atmosphere was made out of thousands of years ago. Hints Imagine looking up into the sky, trying to figure out what the atmosphere up there is made out of. Your only lead: It's raining, a lot. So, the atmosphere must be partly made of rain, and it's just falling down.
readingMnemonic: Turns out, studying the atmosphere is fun ( ふん )! Hints The reading for this kanji is actually the same as one of 分 's on'yomi readings ( ふん ). One trick about complicated kanji is they often take the reading of one of the pieces they're made from. In this case it's 分 . How fun.

meaningMnemonic: If you have a mustache and you hit your forehead on the moon , you’re probably going to break a bone . Ok, so it doesn’t matter so much if you have a mustache, but if you’re travelling fast enough to make it to the moon, you’re definitely breaking a bone if you run into it. Hints Imagine the force and mass of the moon hitting you right in the boney part of your forehead. Whomp! It sure would hurt.
readingMnemonic: Outer space is cold, and if you're traveling to the moon, you're going to need a lot of coats ( こつ ). All of these coats will keep you warm, even if you do end up breaking your forehead bone . Hints Again, feel your bones crack as you smash into the moon. At least you're warm though. Feel the cozy coats you're wearing and snuggle up in their warmth.

meaningMnemonic: The bundle radical and the bundle kanji are the same! Hints Know your radicals, yo!
readingMnemonic: You should always bundle your sock s ( そく ). If you don't, there is a 100% chance you'll lose all of the left ones. Hints Imagine doing laundry and making sure to bundle your socks together so none of them will be lost.

meaningMnemonic: The circumference radical and the circumference kanji are the same! Hints Know your radicals, yo!
readingMnemonic: Practice how to measure the circumference of an item by using your shoe ( しゅう ). Your shoe is kind of round, and it's free. I mean it's right there on your foot. Hints Try to find the circumference of your shoe and then email us with the measurement. I promise you'll never forget this kanji if you actually do it.

meaningMnemonic: The gate to talent is now closed . In fact, the gate to talent is always closed. It's not like anyone can just waltz in and get themselves some talent. You have to work for it! You have to work hard to get through that closed gate to talent! Hints After your hard work, hear the gate close behind you with a creak. You're on the inside now, you're one of the talented ones. And your talents have changed you, made you different from the others — much like the talent radical in this kanji is a little different from its usual shape!
readingMnemonic: Outside the talent gate that's always closed , hay ( へい ) is piled up to make beds for the people who are still trying to get in. Who knows how long they'll be there outside the closed gate, sleeping in the hay, but they're all working hard to become talented. Hints Picture a bunch of people outside the closed gates, sleeping in piles of hay. You were there too once. You know how itchy that hay is, and how cold it can be at night. But it was all worth it.

meaningMnemonic: Next to the cross we combine our power power power so that we have cooperation . And with our powers combined, we become stronger than we ever could have been apart, lifting the cross above our heads! Hints The power of cooperation is a *ahem* powerful thing.
readingMnemonic: Nowhere is the power of cooperation more apparent than in きょう と . When invaders are attacking, when the townspeople want to rebel, when there is a kitty up a tree, the people combine their power from all reaches of Japan and cross into きょうと to put a stop to the madness through cooperation. Hints Imagine being a citizen of きょうと . Watch as the powers from your neighboring prefectures march across the border to come cooperate together to stop the bandits that raided your farm. You admire their cooperation. You admire きょうと !

meaningMnemonic: The leader of the yakuza shows you his knife . He says, "This is an example of a knife." Hints The leader of the yakuza is just showing you an example of a knife. Maybe to scare you? Why would an example of what a knife is scare you, though? Coming from the leader of the yakuza, this is a weird tactic.
readingMnemonic: "This is an example ," the leader of the yakuza tells you. "Next time, I'll show you an example of a ray ( れい ) gun." Hints Why is the leader of the yakuza showing you examples of weapons, not to mention weapons that aren't real, like ray guns?

meaningMnemonic: If your fingers are strong enough, you can take an axe and fold it in half. But be careful not to bend it too far, or you might just break it! Hints Imagine holding an axe between your fingers and folding it like a pretzel. Or some silly putty. Or a really soft axe.
readingMnemonic: Unfortunately, as you fold these axes in half you realize they come in sets ( せつ ), so there are twice the axes you thought there would be. To compensate, you start folding them in sets too. Hints How many axes can you bend at once? A set of two? What about a set of four? Or a set of forty-two?

meaningMnemonic: Crab s in the dirt make a great foundation for a seaside hut. It's right on the seashore, where all the crabs dig their holes in the dirt. But as they get old and die, their bodies form a strong base. Perfect for the foundation of a building like this! Hints Do you live on the beach? Maybe the foundation of your house was made from crabs in dirt too. Why don't you go outside and check?
readingMnemonic: Remember, a good foundation is the key ( き ) to a good house. No, literally. You have to use a piece of the foundation to make the key to your house. Hints Keys to houses are always made out of a piece of the foundation it was built upon. How else would they be unique from one another?

meaningMnemonic: Everyone has a soul in their life , and that soul shapes their gender . It's not just about body parts — it's about what's inside. In the end, it's one's nature that truly matters. Hints Picture your own soul and your own life. Listen to what your soul says about your gender and nature — because your life is yours to live, and only your soul can define who you truly are!
readingMnemonic: Once you've decided what your gender is, someone comes to your house and lays a sa ber ( せい ) on your shoulders. "This is now your nature ," they say, lifting the saber. It's official! It's in all the newspapers, there's a parade, and everyone pats you on the back. Thanks, gender saber! Hints The next time you get one of those surveys where you have to choose your gender, just think back to that time in your life when a random official came and certified your gender with their saber. Ahh, what lovely memories.

meaningMnemonic: A cleat -wearing woman is walking on someone's back, but she doesn't want to hurt him, so she has to be very gentle . Cleats are sharp and pointy, and not designed for back-walking, so she's being extra gentle right now. Hints Picture a woman walking gently over someone's back. She's hardly moving.
readingMnemonic: Actually, the person she's being gentle with is her da d ( だ ). No one would ever want to hurt their dad, especially if he's asked you to walk gently on his back as a way of giving him a massage. Hints Poor old dad. His back hurts so his daughter has to walk on it with cleats to make it feel better. But if she isn't gentle enough, she'll just make it worse.

meaningMnemonic: You give a lid to a person (two of them, in fact), then they put it on a cross when you graduate . It's a symbolic ceremony, putting a lid over a cross, but it's just what you do when you graduate around these parts. Hints Try to picture the lid you give to the person(s), then their putting it on a cross. Why does this ceremony symbolize graduation? Maybe the persons are your teachers, and it's about the divine knowledge you've now finished collecting under your "lid," or something. Congrats?
readingMnemonic: Uh oh, looks like you forgot your lid. They decide not to let you graduate . So two ( そつ ) more years now until you can graduate, it seems. So two more years?! Just for forgetting a lid? Nonsense! Hints Imagine walking up to the stage with no lid, and the person(s) just say, "Sorry, you can't graduate. So two more years. Next!"

meaningMnemonic: A mouth that is old is going to be hard . Hints Go ahead and touch that old man's mouth. It's super hard feeling when you touch it.
readingMnemonic: You touch the old man's hard mouth and it crumbles away, revealing the face of a 子 ( こ ) inside. Hints "You pressed the hard skin holding me captive! Thank you!" the 子 says, as they break free from their hard mouth prison.

meaningMnemonic: Causing death at every turn, the moon king sits inside his moon, getting ready to cause death on anything in his sights. Sounds a lot like the Death Star from a certain movie. One of which is "Star Wars: A New Hope ." Hints Now picture the death moon king as the Emperor, sitting in his Death Star. There is no hope, except for that little opening you can shoot through to destroy the whole thing. That's hope, I guess!
readingMnemonic: The name A New Hope , as we all know, comes from the ending where the moon king's son sends a bow ling ( ぼう ) ball into that little opening and knocks it out of the sky. Hints In the end, the real hope was bowling all along. I hope you've learned a valuable lesson from this space movie.

meaningMnemonic: A tree with talent can become lumber . Not all trees can do this. Only the talented ones are able to turn themselves into lumber or material , to be used for a million different things. Hints Picture a tree standing in the forest. It's thinking so hard you can see the math equations flying around in its branches, until finally a cartoon light bulb appears above its head. This talented tree has figured out how to become lumber!
readingMnemonic: Trees can be turned into all kinds of things, but this one wants to use its lumber and material to build a xy lophone ( ざい ). It's the most difficult instrument to create, so it suits the talent level of this tree! Hints Watch as the tree becomes lumber and that lumber is used to craft a ginormous xylophone. Each key is its own plank of lumber!

meaningMnemonic: You try to be private , but because of your big hair you end up having to participate in everything. Can you imagine people asking for volunteers or something, and you trying to look inconspicuous with your big hair? Of course they're going to notice you and make you participate. Hints When you're thinking about your next hair style, if you don't like participating in things, you should think about something you can actually keep more private.
readingMnemonic: You know who has big hair and loves to participate in everything? San ta-san ( さん )! Well, his hair is more big on the bottom (it's a beard) than whatever you have on your head, but hair is hair. And he participates in present-giving in every house in the world! See? Big hair = participation! Hints Would you want to participate in Christmas if it meant looking like Santa and visiting every single house on earth?

meaningMnemonic: The roof that became the origin of all roofs was perfect . It was tall and wide so it could fit and protect everyone. And the dimensions were perfect too. Hints Picture this absolutely perfect roof. They really got it right on their first try.
readingMnemonic: This perfect roof was commissioned by Genghis Khan ( かん ). We got all of the carpenters and home makers and construction workers he'd conquered together and tasked them with making the first roof, but only if they made it absolutely perfect. Hints Genghis Khan was a perfectionist, and by conquering and bringing all of these different people together, he was able to create something perfect by all standards.

meaningMnemonic: When climbing a tree in public , it’s best to choose a pine . Pine trees offer the most coverage, so you’ll be able to hide, even out in public. Hints Imagine climbing up a pine tree. The pine needles are prickly, so your hands get pricked as you climb. Smell the pine tree smell and feel the pine sap on your hands.
readingMnemonic: In case you fall, someone has laid mats ( まつ ) out around the base of the pine tree. That way, you’ll land on the mats should something unfortunate happen. Hints Picture yourself falling out of this pine tree and onto the mats. The mats are nice and soft so it’s nice. Hear the whoosh of air as you collapse onto the mats.

meaningMnemonic: You tie a thread on your finger before jumping in the pool to remind yourself of the promise you made to your mother. The thread represents the promise you made to mow the lawn after you finished swimming in the pool. Hints The promise reminding thread on your finger was tied too tight. You can feel the thread starting to cut off your circulation as your finger starts to turn purple and go numb. It’s really uncomfortable.
readingMnemonic: After you get out of the pool, you keep the promise you made to your mother. So you get on your yak ( やく ) powered mower and trim the grass. Yes, your mower is pulled by a yak. It’s very efficient. Hints Imagine yourself sitting on a riding mower as you’re pulled around the yard by a yak. The yak is having a hard time pulling you so it's making lots of yak noises. Hear them in your mind.

meaningMnemonic: Yakuza bars barely exist. The remainder of them aren't even in Japan. Hints Imagine a yakuza bar in Zanzibar full of tattooed thugs in colorful swim trunks, all sipping tropical cocktails. No wonder the remainder of the yakuza bars are in Zanzibar — this is a great vibe!
readingMnemonic: The remainder of the yakuza bars aren't in Japan. Strangely, they are all in Zan zibar ( ざん ). Hints Imagine a yakuza bar in Zanzibar. What a strange place to hold out.

meaningMnemonic: The original geoduck had a request . He wants there to be more geoducks in the world! Hints Remember, this is the OG = original geoduck. There are no other geoducks yet.
readingMnemonic: The only person that would even hear the geoduck's request was Gan dhi ( がん ). Gandhi closed his eyes, sat down, and spread the geoduck's request to the rest of the world. Hints People listened when Gandhi said, "My friends. We must stop trying to eat the geoduck, and instead allow it to breed. Join me in this fast!" And that's why we have so many geoducks on the earth today. Thanks Gandhi.

meaningMnemonic: A grain 's child will grow with the seasons . In spring the grain is born, it grows in summer, is harvested in fall, and dies in winter. Hints Watch the grain children live their entire lives throughout the seasons. Though there are 72 seasons in Japan, so the life of a grain is actually really long there.
readingMnemonic: All of the seasons have their own special key ( き ). As they change, that season's key appears and unlocks the next step in the grain's life. Hints Picture these seasonal keys floating through the sky, unlocking the weather changes, the growth of new grains, and the aging of us all.

meaningMnemonic: If a tree wants to kiss you, it's a sign of your status . Only someone of high status would be worthy enough to receive the gnarly but gentle kiss of a tree. Trees don't kiss just anyone, you know. Hints Imagine kissing a tree. Better yet, go kiss a tree. If you're lucky, it'll give you a little taste of sap — an even surer sign of your status.
readingMnemonic: The best way to convince a tree of your status is to say "cock-a-doodle-doo" at it, like a cock ( かく ), i.e. a male chicken. Trees really place a lot of status on the ability to sound like a cock crowing. Hints Probably because a cock crowing means the sun's about to come up. Morning light is basically tree breakfast, after all, and they say the way to a tree's heart is through its chloroplasts. So picture yourself as a cock, cock-a-doodle-doing to a tree about your status.

meaningMnemonic: The best kind of flowers to grow in your window ? Strawberry , obviously. Yes, there are strawberry flowers — it's actually the flowers that turn into the strawberries, you know. And they're perfect as window flowers because they need a ton of light. That's why all your window flowers are strawberries. Hints You don't waste time with non-edible flowers. Only strawberries for your windows. Now imagine that fresh, sweet strawberry smell that would drift in on the breeze every time you opened your windows. Nice, right?
readingMnemonic: Believe it or not, your strawberry is the only cure for an itchy Go dzilla ( いちご ). Hints Imagine Godzilla, covered in an itchy rash, squishing one of your strawberries and rubbing it all over his body to calm his itchy skin.

meaningMnemonic: The origin of the geoduck is a pretty stubborn one. The geoduck race is so stubborn that it refused to evolve into an animal that made any sense. Hence, the origin of the geoduck is one of stubbornness. Hints You know what a geoduck looks like, right? Does that look like a creature that was looking to change and evolve and be awesome? No, geoducks are weird and stubborn. Imagine how stubborn you’d have to be to not want to evolve into a more attractive animal.
readingMnemonic: You know who else was stubborn ? Gan dhi ( がん ). Gandhi believed in non-violent resistance and he was pretty stubborn about it. Hints Gandhi’s stubbornness, however, was pretty effective. Everyone knows Gandhi. Remember Gandhi and his famous stubborn attitude whenever you see this kanji.

meaningMnemonic: The mouth of a well will surround you if you fall into it. The mouth of a well is the opening of the well, and if you fall into that well, the mouth as well as the rest of the well will surround you. Hints Picture yourself surrounded by this well on all sides. You look up and you can barely see the mouth of the well where you fell in and now you are trapped. Imagine how scared you are. Imagine trying to claw your way up the sides of the well but all you do is break your nails on the walls.
readingMnemonic: The well walls surround you as you look up to the mouth once again. This time you see an ea gle ( い ) flying overhead. You call out to the eagle to save you and the eagle comes swooping down into the well and flies you out to safety. What a nice eagle! Hints This eagle is basically a superhero. Imagine an eagle dressed in a superman outfit. He’s your savior. Imagine your gratitude towards this eagle superhero.

meaningMnemonic: A white guy jumps into a pool with a target painted on the bottom. He's aiming for the target, of course. This kanji can also mean -al , as in the endings you get on some English adjectives. You know, like the pool is artifici-al. Or painting a target down there is not practic-al. That kind of -al. Hints Picture this pasty white dude jumping into the target-bottomed pool. The sun glints off of his unnaturally white skin and stings your eyes.
readingMnemonic: This white dude is a huge techie ( てき ) so he has electronic enhancements that make sure he hits the target . Being a techie has its advantages. Hints He hits the water right on target and the water splashes onto you. Since he was a techie, he was able to perform the perfect dive. And now you’re all wet.

meaningMnemonic: You live in the now , so your heart controls your thought process. You don't have time to think with your brain — all your thoughts come straight from the heart. Hints Your heart's thoughts tend to be really spontaneous and emotion-driven: "Follow your dreams! Tell your crush how you really feel! Stop studying kanji and go touch grass!" Wait, no — don't listen to that last thought!
readingMnemonic: What has your heart been giving a lot of thought to lately? Nen doroids ( ねん ). Nendoroids are those plastic anime figurines with the really big heads. You've gotten addicted to collecting them and now they occupy your thoughts 24/7. Hints "Hey, you know what you should do?" says your heart. "You should quit your job and move to Japan to collect nendoroids full-time!" Dangerous thoughts…

meaningMnemonic: The well radical and the well kanji are the same. Hints Make sure you remember that this is a well of water not a "well, actually."
readingMnemonic: Each time you go to the town well , there's a giant ea gle ( い ) hiding inside, just waiting for you to show up. Hints You're absolutely terrified of this giant eagle hiding in the well. You're not even sure what its goal is, maybe it's just out to scare you... Either way, imagine yourself being absolutely terrified of this eagle every time you have to go fetch water from the well.

meaningMnemonic: There is a treasure on top of a narwhal who wears a towel that will grant your greatest wish . Hints Picture this narwhal: above its long horn there is a huge, shiny treasure floating. It pulls the towel tight around itself, "Brururu you found me I see!" it whistles at you.
readingMnemonic: In order to open the treasure and get your wish , you need the key ( き ). The narwhal knows where it's hidden, so you'll have to convince it to tell you where the key is. Hints If you find the key, what will you wish for? Think about your single, greatest wish. Close your eyes and picture it as clearly as you can and you'll find the key.

meaningMnemonic: One animal that is particularly good is the wolf . Wolves have a bad reputation, but actually they're very, very good animals. Hints When wolves are reintroduced to an ecosystem, good things happen. Overpopulation in deer and other animals decline, plants grow and create more habitats, and the balance of wildlife improves. It all starts with wolves, who are good dogs. Also, wolves take care of wild, abandoned kids. Only wolves do that, because they're good. Just ask Mowgli!
readingMnemonic: A wolf might be good, but if you run into one, all you can do is scream Oh 神 !” ( おおかみ ). Hints "Oh 神 ," as in, "Oh god," because you're about to be eaten by a good wolf. You're part of the ecosystem now.

meaningMnemonic: Your ability power is what you can do. This is your ability . It is also your capability .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: コミュニケーション能力
彼女はテレポートの能力を持っています。
sentences.english: She has the ability to teleport.

sentences.japanese: 彼、コミュニケーション能力が高いよね。
sentences.english: He has strong communication skills, doesn't he?

sentences.japanese: この仕事ではどんな能力が求められていると思いますか？
sentences.english: What skills do you think are required for this job?

meaningMnemonic: The kanji means promise , but the meaning of this word is about , which is a little different. Just think about promises. When you promise something you really need to follow through... but only about as much as you need to for the other person to be happy. Someone asks for a puppy for Christmas, and you get them a stuffed animal puppy. It's approximately the promise you made. Close enough. *wink*
readingMnemonic: The reading for this is actually the same one that you learned with the kanji, so no need to memorize anything new!

sentences.japanese: このゴボウの長さは約２メートルです。
sentences.english: The length of this burdock is approximately two meters.

sentences.japanese: 今までで、約百万人の人がトーフグのフェイスブックページに「いいね」をした。
sentences.english: About a million people have liked Tofugu’s Facebook page so far.

sentences.japanese: その会社では約三年間働いていました。
sentences.english: I worked at that company for about three years.

meaningMnemonic: You've probably seen the words 知る and 合う by now. This is someone you "know" because you have "come together" before, but that's pretty much it. You don't really know them well, you just met them a couple times so you know who they are. This person is an acquaintance .
readingMnemonic: The readings are that of 知る and 合う . So long as you know those words, you should be able to read this one too.

sentences.english: to have an acquaintance, there is an acquaintance

sentences.japanese: 知り合いだから、ちょっと聞いてみるよ。
sentences.english: Since I know that person, I'll ask them about it.

sentences.japanese: アイツと知り合いだとはゼッタイにバレたくない。
sentences.english: I absolutely don't want it to be known that I'm acquainted with them.

meaningMnemonic: This is a strange word, I'm afraid. You'll have to bear with it. This, when added onto a word, is like adding an -al or a -like to the end of it—or when something is typical of something else. For example, add it onto 日本 (Japan) and you have "Japanese-like", or "typically Japanese". It's a weird sort of modifying word that really depends on each situation it's in. For now, just know this word means these things. We'll start applying it to various words in the future, slowly but surely.
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji, probably because this is usually added onto other words, making it behave like a jukugo.

sentences.japanese: 自分的には上手にアメリカ的なスピーチができたと思ってたんだけどな。
sentences.english: I personally thought I was able to give an American-style speech pretty well.

sentences.japanese: あのはにかんだ感じのスマイルが、個人的にめっちゃツボなんだよね。
sentences.english: That bashful smile of hers really gets me personally.

sentences.japanese: もう少し具体的に教えてくれませんか？
sentences.english: Could you please give me a bit more specific information?

meaningMnemonic: When you wrap around the entire circumference of the year you've come back around to the start of it. This is the anniversary . This word is commonly used with numbers, like 10 周年 (10th anniversary), or combined with other words, like 周年事業 (anniversary project).
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 周年記念イベントの準備で忙しい。
sentences.english: We're busy preparing for the anniversary event.

sentences.japanese: トーフグは、来年で十周年になるので、コウイチは周年プロジェクトを予定しています。
sentences.english: The next year is Tofugu's 10th anniversary, so Koichi is planning an anniversary project.

sentences.japanese: 明日は私たちが出会ってから、十五周年の記念日です。
sentences.english: Tomorrow marks the 15th anniversary of when we first met.

meaningMnemonic: When you meet for cooperation , you're coming together to help each other. One form of this is when people form association s. They're all cooperating and coming together to help each other and themselves.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: ワニカニ協会の会員になりませんか？
sentences.english: Would you like to become a member of the WaniKani Association?

sentences.japanese: 明日は協会の集まりがあるので、六時に起こしてください。
sentences.english: I have to attend an organization meeting tomorrow, so please wake me up at six.

sentences.japanese: 僕はこの協会で、イベントマネージャーをしています。
sentences.english: I work as an event manager for this association.

meaningMnemonic: The surround ing energy in the atmosphere is what makes up the atmosphere . I love it when it takes three kanji to represent what one of the three kanji already represents.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Note: You'll sometimes hear people say ふいんき , but if you wrote that on a test you'd be marked wrong, so we're sticking with the more standard ふんいき reading. If you need help remembering it, just look a little closer at the kanji — you'll know 雰 is ふん because it gets its reading from the little 分 inside it!

sentences.japanese: このカフェ、いい感じの雰囲気だね。
sentences.english: This café has a nice atmosphere, doesn't it?

meaningMnemonic: When there's nothing but fold s and angle s, you have quite a mess. This word means with trouble because you certainly aren't traversing along a nice, flat piece of space-time, are you? Nah, it's all angled and folded. 折角 is one of those tricky Japanese words that doesn’t have one neat translation in English. The nuance is that something has come about with trouble, either through someone’s efforts, or a stroke of luck. It often implies regret, and is used in situations where you want to express that valuable opportunities, advice, or hard work were in vain for some reason. It’s also used to underline a rare chance that shouldn’t be missed.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Watch out for the せつ changing to せっ , though. Another thing you have to go through with trouble , I'm afraid.

meaningMnemonic: Wood that is lumber is lumber wood . Technically speaking, 木材 is used more for lumber or wood that hasn't been processed yet — less like planks, more like freshly cut lumber still lying on the forest floor. But it's not a hard rule or anything, so don't worry too much about the nuances.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.
